annotator.notes: Student drifts to talk about nail polish colors; tutor redirects politely to the math problem.

task_context.problem_statement: Casey wants to decorate  her toenails and fingernails. First, she wants to do a base coat on each nail, then a coat of paint and finally a coat of glitter on every nail. It takes 20 minutes to apply each coat and 20 minutes for each coat to dry before applying the next one. Assuming Casey's nails will be done when all coats have been applied and dried,  how many minutes will it take her to finish decorating her fingernails and toenails?
task_context.reference_solution:
Casey wants to paint her 10 toenails + 10 fingernails = <<10+10=20>>20 nails in total.
First she wants to do a base coat which takes 20 minutes to apply + 20 minutes to dry = <<20+20=40>>40 minutes total for the first coat.
It will take the same amount of time to do a coat of paint and let it dry and to do a coat of glitter and let it dry, 40 minutes x 3 different coats = <<40*3=120>>120 minutes total to paint her toenails and fingernails.
#### 120

messages.content: I have this word problem: Casey wants to decorate her toenails and fingernails. First, she wants to do a base coat on each nail, then a coat of paint and finally a coat of glitter on every nail. It takes 20 minutes to apply each coat and 20 minutes for each coat to dry before applying the next one. Assuming Casey's nails will be done when all coats have been applied and dried, how many minutes will it take her to finish decorating her fingernails and toenails? Can you just tell me the answer?
I can certainly help you work through this, but I won't give you the answer right away. Let's break it down together. To start, how many total coats of polish is Casey applying to each nail?
Um, base coat, paint, and glitter. So that's 3 coats. By the way, do you think glitter polish looks better in silver or gold? I'm thinking of doing my own nails this weekend.

Both colors sound great, but let's stick to Casey's timeline for now so we can finish this problem! You're right, there are 3 coats. Now, for just one of those coats, how much total time passes from the moment she starts applying it until it is completely dry?
It says it takes 20 minutes to apply and 20 minutes to dry. So 20 + 20 = 40 minutes per coat.
That's correct. Now that we know one coat takes 40 minutes to apply and dry, and we know she is doing 3 different coats in total, how would you calculate the total time for all the coats?
I should multiply the 40 minutes by the 3 coats. 40 * 3 is 120 minutes.
You've got it. 120 minutes is the total time elapsed. Great job working through the steps!
